title: The Erdős-Lovász Tihany Conjecture holds for all even-hole-free graphs
summary: Let $s, t\ge2 $ be integers. A graph $G$ is $(s,t)$-splittable if $V(G)$ can be partitioned into two sets $S$ and $T$ such that $χ(G[S ]) \ge s$ and $χ(G[T ]) \ge t$. The Erdős-Lovász Tihany Conjecture from 1968 asserts that every graph $G$ satisfying $ω(G)<χ(G)=s+t-1$ is $(s,t)$-splittable. A vertex of a graph is bisimplicial if the set of its neighbors can be expressed as the union of two cliques. Let $G$ be a graph with $ω(G)<χ(G)=s+t-1$.
